sentences.text: Paleontologist Charles C. Mook named this genus in 1942.
Its fossils were found in the Nacimiento Formation of the San Juan Basin in New Mexico.
It is classified within the family Alligatoridae.
Scientists believe it likely lived as a generalized predator on the floodplains of the Nacimiento Formation.
Researchers disagree on the precise classification of Navajosuchus within the group Alligatoroidea.
The Paleobiology Database classifies Navajosuchus as a member of the parent group Alligatorinae.
This animal lived from the Danian to the Selandian stages, approximately 66 to 60.9 million years ago.
It was the most abundant crocodilian in the Nacimiento Formation, appearing in both the Puercan and Torrejonian faunal assemblages.
Some research suggests Navajosuchus is a basal member of the family Alligatoridae, specifically within the subgroup Alligatorinae.
Other studies propose that Navajosuchus belongs outside Alligatoridae and Alligatorinae, instead placing it as a basal member of the clade Globidonta.
